events.head: Offshore investment slows
events.text: Oil companies cut back. Offshore suppliers lose contracts; the rest of the economy barely notices.

events.head: Fish-farming rules tighten
events.text: New environmental and licence rules raise costs for fish farms.

events.head: Housing and building slow down
events.text: Fewer new homes are started. Builders and building suppliers must plan for less work.

events.head: A weak krona helps exporters
events.text: Swedish goods are cheaper abroad; imported equipment and parts cost more.

events.head: Baltic freight booms
events.text: Cross-border freight is in demand. Transport firms can fill more trucks if they have drivers.

events.head: Young workers leave for the West
events.text: Some trades struggle to fill jobs. Expect higher wage demands.

events.head: The real falls sharply
events.text: Imported machinery and foreign debt get more expensive; exporters may gain.

events.head: Credit gets tighter
events.text: Banks charge more and lend less. Heavily indebted firms feel it; cash-rich buyers find bargains.

events.head: A crop shock
events.text: A poor harvest raises food prices. Farms gain; restaurants and grocers pay more.

events.head: Industrial exports weaken
events.text: Foreign customers order less from German factories and their suppliers.

events.head: Energy prices squeeze factories
events.text: Electricity and gas cost more. Energy-heavy production is hit hardest.

events.head: Strikes disrupt transport
events.text: A transport strike delays deliveries and keeps customers at home in some cities.

events.head: Tourists shift destinations
events.text: Visitor numbers swing between regions. Hotels and restaurants adjust staff and prices.

events.head: Wages catch up
events.text: Employers compete for skilled workers. Labour costs rise.

events.head: A currency move raises import costs
events.text: Imported equipment costs more; local suppliers gain an edge.

events.head: Electronics parts run short
events.text: A component shortage delays production and deliveries.

events.head: Export demand swings
events.text: Global orders for Korean goods change. Exporters adjust capacity.

events.head: An older customer base
events.text: Demand shifts towards services for older people; youth-oriented businesses lose ground.

events.head: The yen moves
events.text: Imports, foreign debt, tourism and exports all feel the exchange rate.

events.head: Mining slows
events.text: Commodity prices fall. Mining services, transport and regional hotels lose work.

events.head: Bushfire season
events.text: Heat and fires disrupt operations and raise insurance and safety costs.

events.head: The housing market corrects
events.text: Less building and fewer home sales: developers, builders and furniture shops feel it.

events.head: Border delays with the US
events.text: Trade with the US slows at the border. Exporters and their transport partners are hit.

events.head: Port congestion
events.text: Delays at the big ports mean longer deliveries and more stock to hold.

events.head: Warehouse space runs short
events.text: Warehouse rents rise as everyone wants space near the ports.

events.head: A strong tourist season
events.text: Visitors flood in. Hotels, restaurants and leisure fill up; prices can rise.

events.head: Property markets split
events.text: Rents and prices rise in some cities and fall in others.

events.head: The pound swings
events.text: Importers, exporters and anyone with foreign debt feel the move.

events.head: Insurance costs spike in exposed regions
events.text: Premiums jump after a run of disasters.
